'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[November 2021 Pacific Northwest floods]]
**The provincial government of [[British Columbia]], [[Canada]], declares a [[States of emergency in Canada|state of emergency]] in response to ongoing risks from floods and mudslides. Effective immediately until December 1, citizens in affected regions, including the [[Lower Mainland]] and [[Vancouver Island]], are limited to 30 litres of [[Diesel fuel|diesel]] and [[gasoline]] purchased at [[Filling station|fuel stations]]. Vehicles used for essential services, such as emergency response, commercial transport, and public transit, are exempt from this order and granted unlimited access to cardlock gas stations ordinarily used by the commercial trucking industry. [[Price gouging]] at retail gas stations and the resale of fuel is prohibited. Restrictions on non-essential travel along damaged highways are also set in place. [https://globalnews.ca/news/8387091/bc-flooding-mudslides-update-november-19-latest/ (Global News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]]
****[[Austria]]n [[Chancellor of Austria|chancellor]] [[Alexander Schallenberg]] announces a full nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] for the entire population starting on 22 November, amid a surge in new [[COVID-19]] cases that has overwhelmed hospitals. Schallenberg also announces that [[COVID-19 vaccination in Austria|COVID-19 vaccination]]s will become mandatory as of 1 February 2022. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/covid-cases-vaccine-lockdown-austria-b1960671.html (''The Independent'')]
****[[Austria]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 15,809 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,027,274. [https://www.krone.at/2559497 (''Kronen Zeitung'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****The southern [[Germany|German]] state of [[Bavaria]] cancels all [[Christmas market]]s and imposes a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in all [[Districts of Germany|district]]s that have a seven-day incidence rate of over 1,000 per 100,000 people amid a substantial increase in the number of new COVID-19 cases. However, schools and kindergartens will continue to remain open. [https://www.dw.com/en/covid-in-germany-bavaria-cancels-christmas-markets/a-59857041 (Deutsche Welle)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] reports a record 11,289 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 998,488. [https://bbj.hu/economy/statistics/figures/11-289-new-coronavirus-cases-registered-in-hungary (''Budapest Business Journal'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 1,254 deaths from COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 261,589. [https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/73180/ (Interfax)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Canada]]
****[[Health Canada]] approves the usage of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years. [https://globalnews.ca/news/8332426/pfizer-vaccine-covid-children/ (Global News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Grenada]]
****[[Argentina]] officially announces that it will donate 11,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]] to [[Grenada]]. [https://www.memo.com.ar/runrunes/donacion-vacunas-astrazeneca-granada-argentina/ (Memo)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The U.S. [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] authorizes the [[booster dose]] of either [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer]] or [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] for the general public, which means that all adults are eligible to receive their booster dose. [https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2021/11/19/cdc-panel-unanimously-endorses-pfizer-and-moderna-boosters-for-all-us-adults.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
****Restrictions are further eased for [[COVID-19 vaccine|fully vaccinated]] [[Victoria (Australia)|Victorians]] as 90% of adults are now fully vaccinated. Mask wearing is still required in some indoor spaces and limits remain on daily visitor numbers to care facilities. Additionally, unvaccinated people continue to be banned from entering all non-essential businesses and also from employment in many industries. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/nov/19/victoria-is-removing-most-covid-restrictions-for-fully-vaccinated-people-so-what-are-the-new-freedoms (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Palestine–United Kingdom relations]], [[Israel-United Kingdom relations]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] outlaws [[Hamas]], the [[Palestinian militant]] group which serves as the ruling party of the [[Gaza Strip]], and declares the party as a [[List of designated terrorist groups|terrorist group]]. Previously, only [[Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades|the party's armed wing]] was outlawed. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/britain-outlaws-palestinian-militant-group-hamas-interior-minister/ar-AAQTlmq?ocid=uxbndlbing (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[United States racial unrest (2020–2023)|United States racial unrest]]
**[[Kenosha unrest shooting]]
***[[Kyle Rittenhouse]], who shot three people during the [[Kenosha unrest|unrest]] in [[Kenosha, Wisconsin|Kenosha]], [[Wisconsin]], [[United States]], in August 2020, is found not guilty on all counts. [https://www.npr.org/2021/11/19/1057288807/kyle-rittenhouse-acquitted-all-charges-verdict (NPR)]
***Hundreds of people march in [[Chicago]], [[New York City]] and [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]] to [[United States racial unrest (2020–2023)|protest]] the verdict of the trial. [https://newyork.cbslocal.com/2021/11/19/kyle-rittenhouse-verdict-protest-new-york-city/ (WCBS-TV)] [https://chicago.cbslocal.com/2021/11/19/kyle-rittenhouse-verdict-protest/ (WBBM-TV)] [https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/rittenhouse-protest-portland-oregon-declared-riot-81294500 (ABC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Vice Presidency of Kamala Harris]]
**While [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] undergoes medical treatment, [[Vice President of the United States|U.S. Vice President]] [[Kamala Harris]] is transferred presidential power for a short period of time, making her the first female [[acting president of the United States]]. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/annakaplan/2021/11/19/kamala-harris-will-make-history-as-biden-briefly-transfers-presidential-power-during-routine-colonoscopy/?sh=593c232b6a8d (''Forbes'')]
*Iraqi [[Shia]] cleric [[Muqtada al-Sadr]] announces that he is dissolving the [[Promised Day Brigade]], the armed faction loyal to him. Yesterday, al-Sadr said that non-governmental [[militia]]s should hand in their weapons. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iraqi-cleric-sadr-says-he-is-dissolving-armed-faction-loyal-him-2021-11-19/ (Reuters)]
